brief: A salad staircase against a sunny kitchen wall: three rows of three planters stepping up one, two and three storeys from front to back, so the back row does not shade the front. Lettuce seedlings in the front row, young lettuce in the middle row and full-size romaine at the back. Fill every planter with soil and plant it.

requirements.evidence: 9 base cells: front row r=0 level 0 only; middle row r=1 levels 0-1; back row r=2 levels 0-2. check_build clear, overhead look shows all stepped rows.
requirements.requirement: Three rows of three planters stepping up one, two and three storeys front to back

requirements.evidence: 9 drained full-depth bins across the three rows
All 9 bins filled with soil via fill_and_plant, no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL
requirements.requirement: Fill every planter with soil and plant it

requirements.evidence: Front-row bins hold romaine seedlings; visible in default and overhead looks
Middle-row bins hold young romaine; two visible by default, all three visible from above (one occluded from default az45 by taller back-row romaine)
Back-row bins hold harvest-size romaine, visible by default

finish.summary: Built a 3x3 stepped planter staircase (front 1 storey, middle 2, back 3) with 9 drained bins, all filled with soil: romaine seedlings front, young romaine middle, harvest romaine back. Verified clear; overhead view shows all nine plants, one middle plant occluded from the default angle by taller back-row romaine.

lines.label: Edge cap · female, two stories tall
Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
